chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the minimum reward for the one who performs Ziyarah to al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said to me, 'O Abdullah, verily the minimum that will be for him is that Allah will protect him in his self and his wealth until He returns him to his family. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will be the Protector for him.' My father narrated to me (may he be pleased with him) from Saad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee, from Sahl, like his first hadith in the chapter.

key_terms.رَه: Radihahu (May he be pleased with him - referring to the narrator's father)
key_terms.لِزَائِرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The one who performs Ziyarah (visitation) to al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum reward for performing Ziyarah to Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) defines the 'minimum' reward as a dual-layered divine guardianship: preservation of the visitor’s self and wealth during their journey and return, followed by Allah’s direct protection on the Day of Judgment. This establishes the Ziyarah not merely as a ritual but as a covenant of security, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and protective status of the Ahl al-Bayt in both temporal and eschatological realms.
